headline: Ai-Native Data Platform: What's the Real Difference?
description: AI-native vs augmented analytics explained: how an ai-native data platform differs from Gartner's augmented analytics frame, with a 5-pillar comparison.
keywords: ai-native data platform, augmented analytics, ai-native vs augmented analytics, five pillars

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It remains the correct Gartner category for ML-assisted BI. AI-native is a refinement for buyers who need autonomous execution and compounding memory.

mainEntity.name: How does agentic analytics differ from AI-native?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agentic emphasizes multi-step planning. AI-native additionally requires transparency, distillation, multi-entry, and self-correction as first-class features.
AI-native. InfiniSynapse implements all five pillars via InfiniAgent, InfiniSQL, and InfiniRAG.

mainEntity.name: What should I buy first — augmented BI or AI-native agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your team lives in dashboards, augmented BI first. If you run recurring cross-source analyses and lose knowledge when analysts leave, AI-native agent first. Most enterprises need both.

mainEntity.name: Can a BI platform become AI-native?

acceptedAnswer.text: In theory yes, if the vendor rebuilds the workflow around five pillars. Evaluate shipped behavior, not roadmap slides.

mainEntity.name: Does Gartner use the term AI-native?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gartner's primary frame remains augmented analytics and decision intelligence. AI-native is an industry term describing the strict five-pillar subset.
